move: eight cards spring from a core, orbit a tilted ring, fold back
how: A white circular core sits at centre with two faint concentric rings; eight 250px square cards (six photo, two flat colour) are positioned each frame on a tilted elliptical orbit (x = cos*330, y = sin*330*0.42), the front of the orbit larger (scale up to 1.27) and brighter, the back smaller (0.72) and dimmer, z-index swapped by depth. One full revolution takes the whole duration. A spread factor drives the intro and outro: over the first 10% the cards fly out from the core (expo.out) while unrotating from -90deg and fading in; over the last 6% they collapse back to the core (expo.in). Meanwhile the core pops in with back.out(1.8) and pulses scale 1.06 yoyo, the rings expo.out from scale 0.2, and the title/year/footer fade in at 6% and out at 94%; the last frame matches the first.
adapt: Swap the eight card images and captions, the core name and footer strings, the palette of the two flat cards and the stage colour; card count can change (N is derived). Keep the orbit radius:tilt ratio, the one-turn-per-loop rate and the 1s/0.6s spread envelope.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the core, rings and card nodes inside el and reads images/captions from shot. animate(el, shot, D) returns the wrap timeline plus one added tween on a proxy object ({t:0}->{t:D}, ease none, duration D) whose onUpdate runs the orbit placement with gsap.set, so the fx.register seek loop becomes an onUpdate tween on the same timeline. All selectors must be scoped to el; the 540px centre must become el.clientWidth/2 and clientHeight/2.
caveats: orbit is computed per frame via gsap.set in a seek callback, not a tween; port as an onUpdate proxy tween
stacked hue-rotate filters on three cards each frame are mildly costly
